clue.text: See 13
Part of Leonardo's career? As of this year, yes!

definitions.text: Part of Leonardo's career? As of this year, yes!

indicators.note: part of says the letters are a portion lifted from the run of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A wry nod to Leonardo DiCaprio finally winning his long-awaited Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'Leonardo's career'; the whole clue also describes the prize DiCaprio won in 2016, after years of near misses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Award statuette became part of DiCaprio's record when he won Best Actor for The Revenant.

clue.text: Torment soldiers on top of crumbling salient

indicators.note: in a down entry, on top of puts the soldiers above the next piece

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: crumbling means the word salient falls apart and is rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Troops torment the enemy by sitting above a collapsing bulge in the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: To tease someone with something just out of reach is to torment them, after Tantalus of myth.

clue.text: F1 team I involved in online solution?

indicators.note: involved in means the letter I is wrapped up inside the other piece

parts.note: an e-cure is a cure, i.e. a solution, delivered online

explanation.surface: A Formula One outfit asks whether it is caught up in some internet fix.
explanation.walkthrough: E- is the usual prefix for online, so an online cure is E-CURE.
explanation.definitionFit: French word for a stable, used for a motor-racing team such as Ecurie Ecosse.

clue.text: Reaching score playing in the wet? About time

indicators.note: About means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
playing means the words in the wet are performed in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A cricketer reaches a score of twenty batting in the rain, and about time too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges IN THE WET, and 'About' sends those letters around T.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so reaching a score is arriving at the ordinal number after nineteenth.

clue.text: Food flavouring once for you and me

parts.note: thy is the old, archaic form of your, so once used for you
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned seasoning that used to be shared between two people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks an archaic word: THY was the old possessive of thou.
explanation.definitionFit: A herb used in cooking to add flavour, an example of a seasoning.

clue.text: New recruits stationed initially between choppy Nile and another river

indicators.note: between puts the chosen letter in the gap separating the two rivers
choppy water is rough and broken, so the word Nile is broken up and reformed

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of stationed

explanation.surface: Fresh recruits are posted between a rough stretch of the Nile and some other river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choppy' scrambles the first river and 'initially' picks one letter for the gap 'between'; the Tees flows through north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: People who have signed up, especially to the armed forces, are newly enlisted soldiers or recruits.

clue.text: Sensible measure of duvet's inducement to sleep

parts.note: a tog is the unit rating the warmth of a duvet
ether was an early general anaesthetic that put patients under

explanation.surface: How warm a duvet is might decide how easily it sends you to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: TOG is the British unit of a quilt's warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially, someone well organised and level-headed is described as having it all sorted, i.e. sensible.

clue.text: One opposing soldiers in the old uprising

indicators.note: in a down entry, uprising means the letters read upward, i.e. backwards
in places the soldiers inside the other piece

parts.note: ye is the old form of the
men is a common term for soldiers, especially rank and file

explanation.surface: A rebel joins a revolt against troops in some historic uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN 'in' YE gives YMENE, which 'uprising' turns upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A foe or adversary is someone who opposes you.

clue.text: Expression of doubt in the case, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the words in the case might be arranged in some other order

explanation.surface: A lawyer voices uncertainty about a particular legal matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the letters of IN THE CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitation or wavering is a display of uncertainty, so an expression of doubt.

clue.text: Be unhappy about sad tune for a long time

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: to cry is to weep, being unhappy

indicators.note: sad here suggests the word tune is in a sorry, disordered state

explanation.surface: Someone has been miserable over a melancholy song for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sad' rearranges TUNE into ENTU, which CRY goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundred years, used loosely as an exaggeration for ages.

clue.text: Blows knocking one out received by the French drunk

indicators.note: received by means the next piece is taken inside the French article

parts.note: les is French for the (plural)

indicators.note: knocking one out removes a single letter standing for one

parts.note: gales are strong winds, i.e. blows

explanation.surface: A boxer takes punches from the French, knocked out cold and blind drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking one out' takes A (one) out of GALES to leave GLES, which is 'received by' LES.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for so drunk that one cannot stand up.

clue.text: Prepared state feasts within reason? Not feasible

indicators.note: within puts the feasting inside the shortened word
Not signals that the following idea is removed

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion
something that is 'on' is doable or feasible, as in 'that's not on'
to dine is to feast

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether banqueting is reasonable, then rules it impractical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not feasible' works because 'that's not on' means it can't be done; 'within' then houses the feasting in what remains, REAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fully prepared is the condition of being ready.

clue.text: Meeting to hear soprano and tenor

parts.note: to try a case is to hear it in court
S is the abbreviation for soprano in music
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: A rendezvous arranged so that two singers can be listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: A judge hears a case by trying it.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret rendezvous, especially between lovers, is a kind of meeting.

clue.text: Affair affecting one's profile?

parts.note: an extramarital lover is something kept to one flank, and a profile is literally the view of a person from that flank

explanation.surface: A question about whether a scandalous liaison could damage someone's public image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Profile' looks like reputation, but it is the side view of a face; the phrase is the slang for a secret lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang idiom for a lover kept secretly alongside a main partner, so an illicit affair.

clue.text: I'd invested in small amounts after account revealing chance events

indicators.note: after puts the money piece behind the account abbreviation
invested in places the letters of I'd inside the money

parts.note: cents are small coins, so small amounts of money
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An investor's statement reveals small sums put in by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' reads as finance but is the container signal, and 'after' fixes the order; 'revealing' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mishaps that happen by chance rather than design are unplanned occurrences.

clue.text: No groups recalled inviting in venerable Scottish author

indicators.note: inviting means the reversed letters take the next piece in
recalled means called back, so the letters are taken in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
sets are groups
Ven. is the abbreviation for Venerable, an archdeacon's title

explanation.surface: Groups of people were called back into a venerable institution, not otherwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns NO SETS into STESON, which is 'inviting' VEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson, born in Edinburgh, wrote Treasure Island and Kidnapped.

clue.text: Components of antimony final element in stone-cleaning powder

parts.note: the chemical symbol for antimony is Sb, made of S and B
last is the final one, the closing element

explanation.surface: A chemistry lesson on antimony and the last element in a mixture used to clean stonework.
explanation.walkthrough: Antimony's symbol Sb is made of S and B, read as 'S and B'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet of sand driven by air is used to scour grime off building stone.

clue.text: Head of cattle in wrong farm? A small quantity

indicators.note: in places the leading letter inside the wrongdoing

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: Head of takes the first letter of cattle

parts.note: to till is to cultivate land, to farm it

explanation.surface: A farmer finds one head of cattle has strayed onto the wrong farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'farm' looks like a noun but is the verb, to work the soil; 'Head of' and 'in' place one letter within the wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny trace or spark of something, a minute amount.

clue.text: Right down and right-wing?

parts.note: true means correct or right
feeling blue is feeling down

explanation.surface: A question whether being correct and depressed makes one politically conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party, so a loyal Tory is described this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a staunch, loyal Conservative, hence politically to the right.

clue.text: Mostly fresh indications of tree-trunk where trees aren't found?

indicators.note: Mostly means most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: clean means fresh
growth rings in a cut trunk show a tree's age

explanation.surface: Fresh signs on tree-trunks point to somewhere the forest has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter of the synonym for fresh; the question mark flags the playful definition of an open space in woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: Open spaces in a wood, cut free of timber, are gaps in the forest.

clue.text: See 13
Be sorry for others (second going to prison)

indicators.note: going to means the letter departs and is swapped for the next piece

parts.note: the rest means the others
pen is short for penitentiary, a prison

explanation.surface: Regret for the rest, as a second offender is sent to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: In REST, S is replaced by PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel remorse about a wrong done is to regret it, perhaps with contrition.

clue.text: Ignorant fellow caught dipping into SF novel

indicators.note: dipping into means the letter goes inside the novel's title

parts.note: Dune is Frank Herbert's science-fiction novel
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A dim-witted reader is caught leafing through a science-fiction book.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow-witted pupil, the one who once wore a pointed cap in class.

clue.text: Refusal still upset King

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: even means still, as in 'even more'
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A monarch is still put out after being turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the word for still upwards in this down entry, giving NEVE; 'still' here means even, as in 'even better'.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic 'not ever' is a firm refusal.

clue.text: Bribe used around various dates in European parliament

indicators.note: around means the bribe wraps about the next piece

parts.note: a bung is British slang for a bribe

indicators.note: various suggests the word dates in a different form

explanation.surface: Backhanders paid around assorted dates in a European assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges the dates into DESTA and 'around' wraps the slang bribe about them; 'used' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The federal lower house of Germany, a parliament in Europe.

clue.text: Was informed audibly, say, ignoring article giving information

indicators.note: audibly means the word is taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: knew means was informed

indicators.note: ignoring means the next item is left out

parts.note: taken as written
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone learnt something by ear, ignoring an item that was full of information.
explanation.walkthrough: KNEW said out loud gives NEW; SAY 'ignoring' A leaves SY.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of news or gossip, chatty and informative.

clue.text: Inexperienced about receiving information? On the contrary

indicators.note: receiving means one piece takes the other inside it
On the contrary flips the roles, so the information takes in the about word

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A novice wonders about being briefed, and then says the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, RE receives GEN; 'On the contrary' reverses that, so GEN receives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw or untried, as a beginner new to a job is.

clue.text: Welsh composer spurning love — a brief story

indicators.note: spurning means rejecting, so the letter is cast out

parts.note: Ivor Novello was a Welsh composer and actor
love is zero in tennis, shaped as O

explanation.surface: A Welsh composer rejects love, which makes for a short tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivor Novello, Welsh songwriter of Keep the Home Fires Burning, loses an O for love.
explanation.definitionFit: A short novel, longer than a short story, is a compact tale.

clue.text: Expression of joy with position achieved in cycling trick

parts.note: whee is an exclamation of delight
the lie of something is its position, as in the lie of the land

explanation.surface: A cyclist whoops with delight on reaching a pose mid-stunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding a bicycle with the front wheel lifted off the ground is a stunt.

clue.text: Most of journalists retreating in front of doorway, seeing lots of snakes

indicators.note: in front of puts the reversed piece before the doorway
retreating means going backwards
Most of drops the final letter

parts.note: the press means journalists collectively
an entry is a way in, a doorway

explanation.surface: Reporters back away from a doorway on seeing a mass of snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' cuts PRESS to PRES; 'retreating' gives SERP.
explanation.definitionFit: A collective term for serpents, snakes as a group.

clue.text: Country not accommodating Queen's transport

indicators.note: not accommodating means the inner letters are no longer housed

parts.note: terrain is country, as in rough country
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A country refuses to host the monarch's means of travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like a nation, but it is land, TERRAIN; removing ER leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway service is a form of conveyance.
